title: The habit architecture that survives, in 5 images
caption: Willpower is not the system. This is. Five images that show why some habits survive month three and most don't. Save this for the next time you 'fall off'.

promptVars.CONCEPT: The decision is made once in a calm state, not negotiated in the hard moment
promptVars.VISUAL: Two contrasting clean scenes connected by an arrow: a calm still lake (labeled DECIDE) flowing into a storm (labeled EXECUTE), a single steady line cutting straight through both, premium minimal, cream background

promptVars.CONCEPT: A habit you only remember fails — bind it to a mechanism you can't skip
promptVars.VISUAL: A faint thought-bubble labeled REMEMBER dissolving, beside a solid locked gear-and-rail mechanism labeled BIND, the mechanism glowing in the accent color, premium minimal, cream background

promptVars.CONCEPT: A 28-of-30 grid survives a miss; a perfect chain shatters on one
promptVars.VISUAL: Two clean calendar grids side by side: left a fragile chain snapping at one broken link, right a 30-cell grid with 28 filled and 2 empty still labeled WIN, premium minimal, cream background

promptVars.CONCEPT: A slip drops you to half-intensity; full intensity is only re-earned slowly
promptVars.VISUAL: A clean one-way ratchet / valve diagram: an easy fast arrow pointing DOWN to a lower tier, and a slow stepped staircase required to climb back UP, premium minimal, cream background

promptVars.CONCEPT: What you do after a miss matters more than the miss — map the trigger, don't reset
promptVars.VISUAL: A path with a stumble point, and instead of a STREAK RESET button (shown crossed out) a small magnifying glass examining the trigger that preceded the stumble, premium minimal, cream background
